{{Family name hatnote|Ortíz|Bobadilla|lang=Spanish}}
'''Laura Ortíz-Bobadilla''' is a Mexican mathematician specializing in [[differential geometry]], and especially on [[Holomorphic vector bundle|holomorphic]] [[foliation]]s and the [[limit cycle]]s of [[dynamical system]]s. She is a researcher in the Institute of Mathematics of the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM).{{r|unam}}

==Education and career==
Ortíz-Bobadilla is originally from Mexico City.{{r|pun}} She studied mathematics at UNAM, earning bachelor's and master's degrees under the mentorship of {{ill|José Antonio Seade Kuri|es}} and Xavier Gómez-Mont, respectively.{{r|unam}} She completed a PhD in 1991 at the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] in Moscow, Russia; her dissertation, ''Analytic Classification of Complex Linear Vector Fields: Case of Nontrivial Jordan Cell'', was supervised by [[Yulij Ilyashenko]].{{r|mg}}

She has been a researcher in the Institute of Mathematics since 1992.{{r|pun}}

==Book==
With Xavier Gómez-Mont, Ortíz-Bobadilla is the author of a Spanish-language textbook on dynamic systems on surfaces, ''Sistemas dinámicos holomorfos en superficies''.{{r|sdhs}}

==Recognition==
Ortíz-Bobadilla is a member of the [[Mexican Academy of Sciences]].{{r|amc}} In 2020, UNAM gave her their National University Award for Teaching in the Exact Sciences.{{r|pun}}
